title: unit-price-curator-and-autoscale-batcher
author: Ethan Brooks
release_notes: Add Unit Price Curator service and autoscale-aware micro-batcher. Provides tenant-level per-token price signals, autoscale batch size recommendations, and safe quantization profile fallbacks.
description: Summary: Introduce a lightweight service (unit-price-curator) that computes tenant-specific per-token pricing signals and exposes an API used by the autoscale micro-batcher to pick safe batch sizes and quantization presets. Motivation: customers running multi-tenant workloads need predictable unit economics; current autoscalers choose conservative batch sizes or require manual tuning. This PR wires an automated signal path: sample token distributions -> compute effective unit price and variance -> produce recommended batch shape + quant profile and a confidence score. Checklist: - [x] service skeleton + API (gRPC/HTTP) - [x] sampling worker and aggregation pipeline - [x] autoscale micro-batcher integration and decision hook - [x] safe quantization fallback matrix and rollback policy - [x] unit tests for sampling and decision logic - [x] end-to-end smoke test in perf-lab - [x] docs and runbook with operational heuristics Design notes: - Unit Price Curator (UPC) consumes recent token-level telemetry (prefix lengths, model SKU, quant tier) and tenant config. It computes a running weighted median cost-per-1000-tokens and a volatility estimate (sigma). The output is a small JSON recommendation: {batch_shape_hint, target_quant_tier, confidence, reason_tags}. - Autoscale micro-batcher now queries UPC during warm-start and on scaling events. If confidence is high, batcher applies recommended batch_shape within configured latency SLO bounds; if confidence is low, it triggers a conservative fallback and schedules a sampled dry-run. - Quantization: recommendations are conservative by default (e.g., int8 for tested models) and annotated with rollback policy (if output quality regression > threshold, revert). Implementation highlights: - new microservice under services/unit_price_curator with gRPC + HTTP translation layer - lightweight aggregator in telemetry/consumers that keeps a 60m sliding window per tenant - batcher hook in serving/runtime/batcher to request recommendations (async cache for 10s) - a new config flag: autoscale.enable_upc (false by default) Tests: added unit tests for curator math (edge cases for tiny tenants), integration test for batcher reaction to recommendation spikes, perf-lab run that validated no latency regressions for 99th p50-90. Operation: docs/runbooks/unit-price-curator.md contains troubleshooting steps, cardinal alerts (e.g., high volatility, repeated rollbacks), and recommended Linear tickets to open when observed behavior persists. Security: service uses mTLS internally and checks tenant scoping before returning recommendations. Backward compatibility: if UPC is unavailable, batcher falls back to existing heuristics. Migration: feature gated behind autoscale.enable_upc and rollout plan in the runbook. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: noisy telemetry could suggest aggressive quant tiers -> mitigation: a trust-layer that requires min_samples and volatility checks before promoting quant changes. - Risk: increased control plane latency -> mitigation: async cache and 50ms internal timeout. Related: ENG-1382 (tenant pricing signals), PM-402 (autoscale UX improvements).

review_comments: Maya Patel (review): Left a few questions around the volatility threshold and how it's tuned. Also suggested adding a feature flag to force conservative behavior per-tenant.
Ethan Brooks (reply): Added autoscale.enable_upc and autoscale.force_conservative_tenants config; expanded docs with tuning guide.
Jordan Reyes (review): Requested that the batcher not block serving threads when UPC is slow; suggested async cache with a short TTL.
Ethan Brooks (reply): Implemented async cache with 10s TTL and 50ms upstream timeout. Added tests for cache behavior.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified math in unit tests and validated perf-lab run. Approving for merge after addressing one doc wording nit.
Docs owner (review): Nit: clarify rollback probe thresholds. Fixed in docs/architecture/unit-price-curator.md.
notes: Feature gated; ops will enable for a small subset of tenants during initial rollout. Expect gradual enablement over two weeks while monitoring volatility and rollback counts.
